# Assembly guide: Spaceship (FocusPod v2), 2 people, a 5 mm hex drive

| Doc code | Part number | Revision | Status | Date | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2-INS-001 | 100000 POD · Pod hoàn chỉnh | P04 | DRAFT | 2026-10-31 | Packing and Assembly Engineer |

Revision P04 is the pod's own revision: this guide is built on skeleton P04, and the files of part 100000 share one revision (conventions §7 and §8). This is the guide's first issue. It follows the general assembly and the subassembly drawings when they exist and doesn't replace them (guideline §5.1). Labels like **1-05** are the packing labels of [`910000_P01_PACKAGING-PLAN_PKG.md`](../../07-Packaging/910000_P01_PACKAGING-PLAN_PKG.md); every number carries a status (conventions §9).

## Result

1. **Two people, a cordless driver with a 5 mm hex bit and the kit's 5 mm key, {{N_STEPS}} steps: about {{CLOCK_MIN}} minutes ({{CLOCK_PH}} person-hours)** on the layout study's unit times and the PM's rulings of 2026-11-01. That is inside REQ-ASM-01's 4-hour limit; the PM's target for v2 is about {{TARGET_MIN}} minutes (REQ-ASM-01 asks about 1 hour). The timed trial on the prototype decides, and section 6 shows where the time goes.
2. **{{REG_BOLTS}} bolts of the joints register, each captive in its part but the roof grille's 4, which come in a bag with the grille (J-AIR-03): {{N16}} × {{PN16}} (M6 × 16) and {{N25}} × {{PN25}} (M6 × 25) pins and lock screws**, each with its {{PNW}} washer already on. They match the register joint by joint (section 5). Every site fixing is in the register now: the corner keys hook in and DL and DR stand on spigots, with no site bolts (J-BASE-02, J-FRONT-02); the door hinges and the air parts' fixings in DR stay on hold there.
3. **Every part weighs 20 kg or less except the glass** (D-03). The door unit ({{DOOR_KG}} kg) and the fixed glass ({{FIX_KG}} kg) are carried by both people with 2 suction lifters.
4. **Order rules:** all walls before the front; the ceiling closes by order (its side walls' top corner bolts stay finger-tight until both halves are in, R-J9); the door hangs before DT (PM ruling); DR's bolts are driven before the air column stands (J-FRONT-01); every bolt before the linings that cover its bay.
5. **Pictures:** each step that fits parts has a line drawing made from the parts' own CAD on main, outside Fusion, with the drawing generator's exact hidden-line projection: the step's parts black, each with its packing label, and the parts fitted before grey. A part that goes into another is drawn clear of it, with an arrow into place, and an arrow shows any move whose direction matters. A part whose CAD is still to come is drawn dashed from the skeleton's block and marked CAD TO COME. The four renders below show the whole pod.

## 1. Before you start

- **The crew.** Person A leads the lifting and holds each part in place; Person B drives the bolts from inside. Both lift the glass, the long parts and anything overhead.
- **Tools.** The kit supplies one tool, the 5 mm ball-end hex key {{PNKEY}}, in the OPEN FIRST kit (109000, label {{KIT_TAG}}): for the roof grille's 4 bolts, the final check and as a backup (REQ-ASM-03). The installers bring a cordless driver with a 5 mm hex bit long enough to reach through the 19 mm access holes, its clutch set to the joints register's value; the bolt times assume it (the PM's ruling, 2026-11-01).
- **Handling aids** (not tools: ISS-047, ISS-064): 2 suction lifters (two-cup, each rated 40 kg or more; assumption), 2 step stools with 2 treads, a 600 mm spirit level, a utility knife for straps and film, cut-resistant gloves and safety shoes.
- **The room:** see the [install sheet](100000_P04_POD-INSTALL-SHEET_INS.md): at least {{ROOM_H_GUIDE}} mm clear height, a floor flat within the glides' range, a door at least 810 mm wide (REQ-ASM-06), room round the 2500 × 1700 footprint to lay the parts out, and a 120 V, 60 Hz wall outlet (NEMA 5-15, 15 A) within reach of the pod's cord (D-133).
- **Directions:** left and right as seen from outside, facing the door (conventions §4). Position codes: walls L1 and L2 (left, lower and upper), R1 and R2 (right), B1 to B4 (back: lower left, lower right, upper left, upper right); ceiling C1 (left) and C2 (right); decor blocks DL, DR, DT.
- **The clock** (REQ-ASM-01; its start and stop are PROPOSED): it starts with the pallets unwrapped on site and stops with the pod closed, powered and the fans running, after the final check (step {{STEP_FINAL}}). Step {{STEP_LEDGE}} fits the ledge after the clock.

## 2. Safety

- **Glass.** The door unit is {{DOOR_KG}} kg and the fixed glass {{FIX_KG}} kg: always both people and both suction lifters. Check each lifter's vacuum before every lift. Get each pane upright by tilting it up in the crate on its padded long edge, both lifters at its top edge, onto the padded glass rest; never lift a pane flat and never turn it on a corner. Carry glass upright, never flat and never over anyone. Set it down only on the padded glass rests or in its channel, never on a corner or a hard floor. Leave the protective film on. The glass stays in its crate until its step.
- **Weight.** Every other part is 20 kg or less (D-03); parts longer than 1.6 m or heavier than 15 kg are carried by both people.
- **Height.** Never two people on one step stool. The ceiling halves, the soffit, its cartridge, DT and the ceiling linings are lifted by both people, each on a stool of their own, onto a rest, and let go before anyone fixes them: no one holds a part overhead to fix it (the PM's ruling, 2026-11-01). For the other high work, one works from a stool and the other hands up.
- **Hands.** Keep fingers off the joint faces while a panel is lowered onto its spigots and while a bolt pulls a seam shut.
- **Bolts.** The cordless driver, its clutch set to the joints register's value (the Joints Engineer's, with margin against the rivnut spinning out; the torque is on HOLD until the rivnut test T06, HOLD-01, D-48): drive until the seam closes onto its stop and the clutch slips. No impact drivers, no extension bars.
- **Electrics.** Power stays off until step {{STEP_POWER}}, when the pod's cord goes into the room's 120 V wall outlet (D-133). The mains side comes wired from the factory on its tested plug-in harness (D-87): nothing is wired on site, and everything inside runs on 12 V (D-10).
- **Packaging.** Hold a strap while cutting it. Keep film and foam off the walking area.

## 3. How the joints work (read once)

- **Captive bolts.** Each bolt sits in the edge tube of the part placed second, with its washer, pulled back and held by a grommet (joints register 2.2). You only turn it: the driver's 5 mm bit (or the kit's key) goes through the Ø19 hole from the 60 × 60 fill pocket in that panel's bay. The one exception is the roof grille: its 4 bolts go in from the roof with their washers (step {{STEP_ROOF}}, J-AIR-03).
- **Spigots.** Every wall and ceiling part stands on two Ø8 spigots, a round hole at one end and a slot at the other, before its first bolt (REQ-ASM-04). If a part doesn't drop on, lift it and seat it again; never force it.
- **Two bolts, one key.** {{PN16}} (M6 × 16) for the {{N16}} other bolts: each pulls its joint onto its 2.26 mm metal stop or its seat. {{PN25}} (M6 × 25) pins at the 10 closing-seam positions (B1–B2, B3–B4, C1–C2): snug only, they hold the faces level and pull nothing (joints register 2.10). Two more lock the soffit on its hanger studs (J-AIR-01).
- **Order of tightening** (joints register 2.7, R-J9): closing-seam pins first, then the stopped seams; the side walls' top corner bolts and the ceiling's side bolts last, once both ceiling halves are in.
- **Linings last.** Every bolt is driven through a bay that a lining cassette covers later, so check each wall's bolts before its cassette goes on.

## 6. Time

{{TIME_TABLE}}

Each step's time is its 2-person work plus half its 1-person work (shared between the two), plus 15% for hand-offs, the layout study's model (`scripts/assembly.py`). Where the time goes:

{{TOP_STEPS}}

**The PM's rulings of 2026-11-01 on the next five time sinks cut the clock from {{CLOCK_BEFORE}} minutes to the {{CLOCK_MIN}} above:** the installers' cordless driver for the bolts ({{SAVE_DRIVER}} min), a rest for each overhead lift so no one holds a part overhead to fix it ({{SAVE_REST}} min), and the final check split between the two people ({{SAVE_SPLIT}} min); the unit times are assumptions until the timed trial. Lift-off hinges set in the factory (FRONT, in the hinge HOLD's asks, D-138) and a plug-in light shelf (ELECTRICAL's connector choice) would save about 7 minutes more (assumption), to about {{CLOCK_NEXT}} minutes against the PM's target of about {{TARGET_MIN}}. Carrying and unpacking have no cheap fix, and hook-in wall joints, which getting near 1 hour would need, are a redesign the PM ruled out for now.

**D-87 (PM, 2026-10-31) cut the clock from 168 minutes (PR #52) to 127 (PR #59).** The PM took four of the five fixes priced on that model, and they are in the steps now:

| Fix | Steps | Priced on the 168-minute model | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| The exhaust fan box fitted inside the soffit and the intake riser joined to the supply fan box at the factory, plug-in connectors, tool-free hooks for the soffit and the column, one hinged soffit underside | {{STEP_RISER}}, {{STEP_COLUMN}} and {{STEP_SOFFIT}} | 11.4 min (calculation) | AIR (CEILING Engineer), FRONT |
| Glides preset at the factory, corner keys that hook in (12 fewer bolts), band pieces that locate on the keys | 2 | 11.8 min (calculation) | BASE, Joints Engineer |
| The floor foam bonded under the floor panels at the factory (D-132 then removed the floor), and every pallet 2 part set down at its place in step 1 | 1 and every carry | 10.7 min (calculation) | Packing, BASE |
| A factory-tested plug-in harness and a self-test button on the hub | {{STEP_ELECTRICS}} and {{STEP_POWER}} | 8.1 min (calculation) | ELECTRICAL |

The fifth, moving the film peeling after the clock, was rejected so the number stays honest. Instead the film covers only the {{FILM_FACES}} faces that show (the 8 wall skins, the 3 decor blocks and both faces of both glass panes; none on the roof skins) and each panel has a quick-release tab. Peeling now takes about {{FILM_MIN}} minutes of the clock, against {{FILM_ALL_MIN}} for film on all {{FILM_FACES_ALL}} faces without tabs: {{FILM_SAVES}} minutes saved. The layout study's 168 minutes didn't count film at all, so this is time the clock now carries honestly.

The 1-hour target needs more than this: the timed trial showing faster unit times than the layout study assumed, or fewer loose pieces and bolts. The {{REG_BOLTS}} register bolts alone take about {{REG_BOLT_MIN}} minutes of the clock. For scale, hushMeet takes 2 installers 2.5 to 3 hours (source: the market study, as the layout study §4 quotes it).

## 7. Final check list (step {{STEP_FINAL}})

- [ ] Door: swings out to 90 degrees and back with no rub; 4 mm under DT along the head; kick strip level with the band's bottom edge, about {{DOOR_GAP}} mm over the room floor (D-132); closes onto DT's magnetic catch 368007 and stays shut (no lock, D-83); the drop seal comes down onto the room floor when closed; both end brushes stand on the floor along their whole length and close against the end plates beside them.
- [ ] Seals: with the pod lit and the room dark, no light at any seam, at the door's edges or at the fixed glass's edges.
- [ ] Bolts: all {{REG_BOLTS}} register bolts driven, the 10 pins snug, the 6 upper corner bolts tightened after the ceiling; the other fixings of section 5 done.
- [ ] Linings: all 10 cassettes on their clips, both ceiling cassettes on their safety catches, none touching anything but its clips.
- [ ] Air: both fan pairs run; air leaves the kick grille at the column's foot and enters the soffit grille; boost works; the hub shows CO2.
- [ ] Lights: the light shelf works in every scene, including 'call' (D-70).
- [ ] Film peeled from the ACP and the glass; packaging off site, but the seam prop stays with the pod (taking the ceiling down needs it); floor clean.

## 8. Taking it down

Unplug the pod's cord first. Then the reverse order: ledge; ceiling linings (unhook the catches first); soffit underside, exhaust fan box, exhaust cartridge, soffit; air column front face, supply cartridge, air column (it must come out before DR's bolts can be reached, J-FRONT-01); R1's and R2's cassettes off their clips first (DR's inner face can't come off past them, the PM's ruling), then DR's inner face, supply fan box, intake riser; the other wall linings; DT; the door; DR, then the fixed glass with both lifters; DL; the ceiling: first stand the seam prop on its foot under the seam's front end (it holds both corners), then loosen the side walls' top corner bolts, take out the edge bolts and last the 4 seam pins, and lift C2, then C1, off the wall tops and the prop; the upper walls, the lower walls; base band: FR1 off the rail first, then the rail, FL2 and FL1, each lifted 10 mm and drawn back off its studs; the back band lifts straight up out of the side bands' studs once B1 and B2 are off (J-BASE-02). Pack by the labels, into the same places.
